newsitem.title: USA: Baltimore copper stocks seen as arbitrage play.
newsitem.headline: Baltimore copper stocks seen as arbitrage play.

text.p: The sudden increase in copper stocks in Baltimore appears to be part of an arbitrage play, but also offers an indication to the weakness in demand in the U.S., dealers said.

In the last three trading days, 2,267 tonnes have flowed into the COMEX Baltimore warehouse and 2,325 tonnes have entered the LME warehouse in Baltimore from South America. Depending on which way the arbitrage between the LME and COMEX prices move, material will simply be trucked between the two warehouses.
But that the metal was parked in the warehouse rather than a consumer is a testament to how weak demand is from the consumers, dealers said.

"Demand is very dull," said one physical trader with ties to South America. "This is likely unsold copper. And there's nothing else they can do with it, so they move it into the warehouse and they play the arbitrage."
The LME cash price was trading at a 4.60-cent premium to the COMEX spot price at 0951 EDT, up from 0.95 cent Friday. A week ago, COMEX spot was at a 1.15 cents premium to LME cash.
"You don't ship copper to a warehouse if you have a customer for it," said one brass mill executive. "The fact that the copper is showing up in warehouses must mean there's plenty of copper around."
The spot merchant premiums are unchanged at 2.25-2.50 cents over the COMEX cash price.
((--Derek J. Caney, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1646))
